data.title: Flesh out memphis/BRANDING.md: Memphis Group palette, CSS fill patterns, design vocabulary

data.body:
Review (inline, not a fresh-context sub-agent — this session is configured against spawning sub-agents; noting so the log is not read as a full review-gate pass).

Verified by rendering, not by inspection: drove the Playwright chrome-headless-shell already on this machine against memphis/index.html.

Findings, both fixed:
1. CORRECTNESS (caught by render): the brief's central pattern mechanism was wrong. It shipped gradient fills as :root custom properties (--pat-stripe etc.) claiming nested var() resolves against the referencing element. It does not — var() inside a custom property is substituted at computed-value time on the element where the property is DECLARED, so :root baked in :root's --pat-ink and every override was ignored. The hero sunburst rendered black instead of yellow. Isolated with a minimal probe (custom-property form -> rgb(255,0,0) from :root; class form -> rgb(0,255,0) from the override). Fixed by shipping all patterns as utility classes in both the brief and the page, with the trap written up as a blockquote in BRANDING.md so it is not reintroduced.
2. Brief self-consistency: the links and accent bands both sat on Paper, violating the brief's own 'adjacent bands never share a ground' rule. Links band moved to Du Pasquier Powder.

Also revised the Bacterio and terrazzo SVGs after seeing them tile — the first pass read as uniform rings and an even chip grid rather than Sottsass's varied marks. Both now use varied stroke weights / chip sizes.

Verification run: all 4 SVG data URIs parse as XML and survive percent-decode round-trip; every class used in markup is defined; no unclosed tags; scrollWidth == clientWidth at 320/390/768/1440 (no horizontal scroll); desktop and mobile renders inspected.

Acceptance criteria met: 13 named swatches with hexes and roles; 11 reusable fill patterns (5 gradient, 4 multi-layer, 4 SVG — grid/bacterio/terrazzo/wave/fan applied on the page); contrast table computed rather than asserted; no external requests (system font stack, data URIs only).

Meets acceptance criteria. No rework needed.
